newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to allow foreign ships to sail to China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to allow foreign ships to sail to China.

text.p: Taiwan's transport ministry said on Tuesday it would propose allowing foreign-registered container ships to sail between Taiwan and China via a third port.
The liberalisation, not yet completed, would need approval by the cabinet before taking effect, a ministry official said.
Under current restrictions, foreign companies wishing to transport cargoes between Taiwan and China have to change ships at a third port.
"The measure would facilitate the operation of foreign shipping companies, and encourage them to choose Taiwan as part of their routes," the official said.
The ministry has no plans to extend the liberalisation to Taiwan-registered ships, the official said.
Taiwan has banned all direct contacts with China since the two were separated after a civil war in 1949. All links must be routed through a third country.

But the island has recently been exploring ways to ease the ban without compromising the sovereignty of its exiled Republic of China government by recognising China's communist government -- an essential concern.

In 1995, Taipei devised a plan to set up "offshore transshipment centres" at its major ports, allowing cargoes to be transshiped between China and third countries without passing through Taiwan customs. Taiwan cargoes would not be shipped from the centres to China, however.
China has rejected the plan, instead proposing direct shipping links between the two sides.
Taiwan has responded coolly to Beijing's proposal.
